data.description:
## Problem
`workflow/steps.py::GATE_POLICIES` (`default`/`strict`/`advisory`) fails a workflow step by
exact string membership of `finding["severity"]` in a fixed list (e.g. `["critical", "high"]`
for `default`). This is the same impact-only signal the epic is retiring, and since
`severity` is derived from impact alone while the real BLOCK decision already uses
`priority = validity x impact >= block_threshold`, the two gates can disagree on the exact
motivating bug: a high-impact/low-validity finding trips `fail_on_severity` while `priority`
says it should not block.

## Approach
Replace each policy's `fail_on_severity: [...]` list with a `priority_threshold: float | None`
(`None` means never fails, matching today's `advisory` policy):
- `default`: reuse `review_kernel.decide.DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` (the same single source of
  truth `pass3_decide` uses for its own BLOCK decision) rather than a second hardcoded number.
- `strict`: a lower threshold than `default` (catches more) -- `DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` minus
  a fixed documented margin, so it stays strictly stricter than `default` without a second
  magic constant.
- `advisory`: `priority_threshold: None` (never fails), matching today's empty
  `fail_on_severity: []`.
Update the `gate` step (`steps.py:215-239`) to compare
`finding.get("priority", 0.0) >= policy["priority_threshold"]` instead of the severity
membership test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `GATE_POLICIES` in `workflow/steps.py` has no `fail_on_severity` key remaining; each
  policy has a `priority_threshold` key (`float` or `None`).
- [ ] The `default` policy's threshold equals `review_kernel.decide.DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD`
  (imported, not duplicated as a literal).
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_steps.py` passes with `test_gate_fails_on_high_severity`,
  `test_gate_strict_fails_on_any_finding`, `test_gate_advisory_never_fails`, and
  `test_gate_unknown_policy_falls_back_to_default` rewritten to construct findings with a
  `priority` value instead of a `severity` string, asserting the same pass/fail behavior for
  equivalent priority values.
- [ ] A new test proves the config-effect contrast: the same finding (fixed priority) gates
  differently under `default` vs `strict` vs `advisory`, run through the real `gate` step.

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit test against the real `gate` workflow step function. Oracle: the
step's returned pass/fail verdict for a finding of a given priority, under each named policy.
Config-effect contrast (test-design.md sec.6): run the same finding through `default` and
`strict` and assert the outcomes differ where priority sits between the two thresholds.
data.title: Migrate fail_on_severity workflow gate to a priority threshold
